items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: Sometimes I’d go to the Ray Ban stage and that was the rhythm & blues with Dr. John and Alan Toussaint and people like that

ctx.x: You just show up and the music’s there and you’ve got to nail it, right?

Right. You’ve got to read it. That’s what I’m saying about being a reading musician, you could react when there’s written music or I’ve done a lot of sessions where there was no music, you had to just do it from here. Or sometimes they gave you the part from the piano and you put it together. And to be able to do it all, man, means that you are able to do more things. Like in New Orleans at the Jazz and Heritage Festival back in the days when I was playing quite a bit, sometimes I’d play in Economy Hall which is…
Is that the hardest part — well let me rephrase — what’s the hardest part for you to teach to younger players about improvising or music in general?
